name: Bakery House Creek (ベーカリーハウス クリーク)

claims.text: Full wheat bakery (~80 wheat breads baked and sliced daily on-site) sharing space with the rice-flour line — realistic airborne wheat-flour and shared-equipment cross-contact. OPTIONS tier only.
Vegan-friendly 米粉100％ loaf is baked in the same premises as dairy/butter wheat breads; no separation stated.
No formal allergen-handling protocol published; GF items are recipe-based (卵・乳製品・小麦粉不使用) rather than contamination-controlled. Ask staff which items are 米粉100％.
Genuine, clearly labelled 米粉100％ gluten-free line: 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン made 卵・乳製品・小麦粉を一切使わず, plus rice-flour bagels, cookies and cheesecake.

Shop advertises グルテンフリー as a product/ingredient claim but is a full patisserie also making wheat-flour items (roll cakes, baumkuchen, sandwich cookies); no no-wheat-on-premises or cross-contact statement found.
Many cakes contain dairy and eggs; vegan applies only to specific chocolates/raw items.
No published allergen-handling protocol; buyers must confirm per-item and about shared equipment directly.
"白砂糖・添加物を使用しないチョコレート" and "グルテンフリーやオーガニックカカオといった素材にもこだわり"; sells 米粉ケーキ.
米粉シフォンケーキ専門店 making only rice-flour chiffon; 国産米粉100%. Low likelihood of wheat on-site, but no explicit no-wheat-on-premises statement published, so cross-contact is unconfirmed.
Base uses 豆乳/米油/きび砂糖, but some flavors use 牛乳 (dairy) and cream sandwiches use whipped cream.
Owner-run micro takeout stand; contact via Instagram/LINE to confirm allergen/kitchen details.
"小麦粉だけではなく添加物は極力使わず"; 油は米油、砂糖はきび砂糖、国産米粉100%.
"添加物は極力使わない、安心安全な米粉スイーツ".
Small takeout counter that also sells non-GF ライトミール from the same counter; shared prep space means cross-contact is possible.
Dessert/drink focus; no wheat soy sauce implicated in the signature items.
Chocolate flavor contains some dairy: 「ショコラのチョコレートの中には一部乳成分が含まれます」.
Signature ソイシュークリーム explicitly labeled 乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー with a 米粉 (rice-flour) choux base.
Small general fried-chicken shop; a shared fryer is likely. Guide states wheat on-site is limited to burger buns and beer, but fryer/seasoning cross-contact is unconfirmed — ask before ordering.
Sauces/glazes (yangnyeom, teriyaki-style) may contain wheat soy sauce; confirm per item.
Offers a paid GF bun swap (+¥200), indicating some allergy awareness, but no formal cross-contact protocol documented.
米粉チキン専門店です。米粉チキンは、小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使っており、グルテンフリーです — rated ★★★★ by JP GF guide.

Own claim of 完全グルテンフリー化: the production factory and shop were rebuilt in Oct 2023 to be entirely gluten-free, and all products are marketed as 全商品グルテンフリー — implying no wheat is handled on-site, so cross-contact risk is minimal.
Corroborated: 豆乳などを活用することで全商品グルテンフリーの身体に優しいパティスリー.

Signature 「SOY豆乳醤油プリン」 is served with a 醤油 (soy-sauce) caramel; ordinary soy sauce contains wheat. Given the facility's stated complete gluten-free conversion they would be expected to use a wheat-free tamari, but this is not explicitly documented — confirm directly for celiac safety.

Kitchen uses no dairy in cakes (豆乳 substitutes milk) and offers wheat/dairy/egg-free lines, reducing animal-product contact, but eat-in afternoon-tea and some savory items are not confirmed fully vegan.
Deep allergen literacy: shop developed 29-allergen-free (29品目アレルゲン物質除去) cakes and frames itself around 食のバリアフリー for allergy sufferers since 2009.
One of very few fully gluten-free-converted production facilities in Kyoto, purpose-rebuilt in Oct 2023.
Card / e-money / QR payments accepted; parking and eat-in café available.

name: THE NICOLE / Nicole Naturelle (ザ・ニコル / Nicole Naturelle)

claims.text: The Nicole Naturelle allergen-free sweets are baked in the same premises as THE NICOLE's conventional wheat-flour cakes and a wheat-roux European-style spice curry, so shared-kitchen cross-contact with wheat is a genuine risk despite the rice-flour recipes.
Venue's own claim for the line: 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』／『グルテンフリー』／国産米粉100%. No dedicated-facility or cross-contamination protocol is stated.
Not applicable to the sweets line; however the shop's spice curry is not part of the gluten-free line and should be assumed to contain wheat (欧風カレー roux) — do not treat curry as GF.

Nicole Naturelle items are made in a kitchen that also handles dairy, eggs and animal fats for conventional cakes; the Naturelle line itself is 卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用 but shared equipment means trace animal-product contact is possible.

The shop positions itself as making 「食材の制限がある方も楽しめるスイーツ」and takes Naturelle items ご予約のみ (by reservation), suggesting allergy awareness, but no formal celiac cross-contact handling procedure is documented.
Explicit written wheat-free claim using 100% domestic rice flour: 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』『グルテンフリー』, a dedicated recipe line rather than incidental GF items.
Naturelle line is fully vegan (京豆腐, 豆乳ヨーグルト, ココナッツオイル), doubling as a good option for plant-based celiacs.

OUBON is a conventional pâtisserie that handles both wheat cakes and rice-flour cakes: 「通常の小麦を使ったケーキや洋菓子、グルテンフリーなケーキやスイーツなどを扱っているお店」. Shared wheat kitchen means airborne-flour and shared-equipment cross-contact risk; not celiac-safe.
Not applicable — this is a dessert/patisserie shop; no savory soy-sauce dishes on offer.
GF items are not vegan by recipe — egg (卵) and dairy (乳) are listed as allergens on the rice-flour products, so vegan cross-contact is moot.

The shop markets the rice-flour line as 「アレルギー対応の米粉ケーキ」 (allergy-conscious rice-flour cakes) and states allergens for the roll as egg and dairy, indicating some allergen awareness, but no dedicated-line or celiac protocol is claimed.

A named, clearly-labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー range (roll, financiers, madeleines, shortcake, lemon cake) with rice flour sourced from Asahi Seifunjo, made by a 40-year-veteran chef — a convenient wheat-free sweet stop right by Fushimi Inari.
